abstract: Muscle satellite cell (MuSC) differentiation into myoblasts underpins skeletal muscle regeneration by supporting myofiber repair and formation. This process involves extensive metabolic remodeling from glycolysis to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Although this switch is required for proper MuSC differentiation, its molecular regulators remain unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial carrier homolog 2 (MTCH2) as a regulator of this remodeling. MTCH2 contributes preferentially to MuSC differentiation rather than proliferation and supports mitochondrial respiration, particularly under a low-glucose condition. Loss of Mtch2 fragments mitochondria and suppresses respiration associated with fatty acid {beta}-oxidation. Notably, MTCH2-dependent fatty acid utilization appears largely independent of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 (CPT1). Furthermore, skeletal muscle regeneration is impaired in MuSC-specific Mtch2 conditional knockout mice. Together, these findings establish MTCH2 as a regulator of mitochondrial metabolic remodeling in MuSCs and highlight its context-dependent roles in cellular metabolism and function.
